headline: Election eve: Berlin Linke 22% vs CDU 20%; MV SPD 37% vs AfD 36%; Denmark/Greenland push back on Trump “permanent control”; BVB 0–0 HT at Stuttgart.

stories.title: Election eve: Berlin Linke–CDU photo finish; MV SPD edges AfD 37–36 — polls open Sunday 08–18

facts.text: Parties wrapped campaigns Saturday ahead of Sunday votes in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern; polls 08:00–18:00; first-time 16-/17-year-old franchise in both (DLF / NDR).
Berlin ZDF-Politbarometer Extra (FG Wahlen, 14–17 Sep, n=1,611): Linke 22%, CDU 20%, AfD 18%, Grüne 15%, SPD 12%, BSW 4%; 23% still unsure; CDU–SPD Senate would lack a majority (ZDF).
MV Politbarometer Extra: SPD 37% (+3) vs AfD 36% (−1); Linke 9, CDU 6, Grüne 5, BSW 4 — SPD–Linke incumbent pair also short of a clear majority on paper; Schwesig preferred MP 61% vs Holm 30% (ZDF).
Housing/rents dominate Berlin campaign framing; MV race framed as Schwesig polarization vs AfD after a late SPD bounce (ZDF).

stories.whyItMatters: Overnight’s fuel package was the campaign closer — tonight the ballots are set for two of Germany’s most watched Land races, both within error margins.

stories.title: Denmark & Greenland: US Arctic deal will not cede sovereignty — details still opaque

facts.text: Saturday statements from Copenhagen and Nuuk stress any US deal respects Kingdom sovereignty and Greenlanders’ self-determination after Trump claimed “permanent control” over security “and all other needs” (Guardian).
FM Løkke Rasmussen: hope UNGA week yields a binding Arctic/NATO-security pact that still respects the Kingdom’s red lines; Greenland PM Nielsen echoed sovereignty language (Guardian).
Key unknowns remain public: scale of US presence and whether any formal foreign-policy/resource authority shifts to Washington; NATO spokesperson welcomed the framework (Guardian).

stories.whyItMatters: Morning’s deal announcement is intact — Saturday’s pushback is about framing and red lines before next week’s UNGA signing.

stories.title: Stanford Medicine: human “brain” is two organs — hindbrain from a separate progenitor

facts.text: Nature Neuroscience (18 Sep): fore/midbrain (Otx2) and hindbrain/brain-stem (Gbx2) arise from mutually exclusive progenitors with distinct chromatin — not a single early progenitor as long assumed (Stanford Medicine).
Team grew functional human hindbrain motor neurons in vitro for the first time; pattern conserved back to chickens, zebrafish and acorn worms (~550 Myr) (Stanford).
Aim: better models for SMA/ALS and other brain-stem diseases where living tissue is unavailable; HN ~500 pts overnight (Stanford / HN).

stories.whyItMatters: Explains decades of failed hindbrain-in-a-dish attempts — and opens a concrete regenerative-research path.
